ut_grand_staircase.blurb: Grand Staircase is a spread-out set of small climbing areas inside Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument in south central Utah, reached from Highways 89 and 12. Sport and trad are split almost evenly, with a handful of boulder problems and a single top rope. Most climbs fall between 5.7 and 5.11, with a few easier and a few harder. Much of the monument's rock is soft sandstone, but Buckskin Gulch is limestone, mostly vertical with the odd bulging overhang. It holds the most climbs, and the cooler months are preferred there. Church, The Desert Wedding Site, Long Canyon and Cannonville Area each add a smaller number of climbs.

az_cochise_campground_vicinity_boulders.blurb: These boulders sit in the East Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, in the Dragoon Mountains of southeastern Arizona, around the campground and along the Cochise Trail. Nearly everything is bouldering, spread across every level from the easiest problems into the double-digit V grades, with plenty of easy and middle grades. The stone is granite, streaked with green and grey lichen, and it ranges from abrasive to slick. Cochise Trail Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by Campground and Walk of Nature Loop Boulders. First Streambed has only a few problems, in a stretch where getting between boulders takes some scrambling.

ca_rainbow.blurb: Rainbow sits just off Interstate 80 near Big Bend, on the west side of Donner Pass between Cisco Grove and Kingvale. Bouldering makes up most of the climbs, alongside trad, sport and top rope on a small crag, all on granite. Boulder problems run from V0 into the V11 range, and Trigantor and Sugar Cube are known for highball problems. The crag's routes are mostly 5.9 to 5.12, on thin edges and cracks across small dome-like features. Its wall faces west, so spring and fall suit it best, and the boulders are reachable May through November in most years. Main Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by Trigantor and Central Area.

ca_west_rim_area.blurb: West Rim Area is the left-hand rim of the Happy Boulders, in the Volcanic Tablelands about seven miles north of Bishop, California. Every climb is a boulder problem, spread from V0 up to V11 with a solid base of moderates. The Happy Boulders as a whole are volcanic Bishop Tuff, which looks crumbly but is surprisingly solid. This rim stays shady and cool compared with the rest of the Happies. Clapper Area and Toxic Avenger Area hold the most climbs, with Hand to Hand Combat Area and Sabres of Paradise close behind. At Hall of Mirrors Area the problems are mostly moderate, with flat landings.

co_rampart_range_bouldering.blurb: Rampart Range Bouldering is a collection of boulder clusters scattered along Rampart Range Road in Colorado's South Platte area, reached by heading west from Sedalia on Highway 67. Every climb is a boulder problem, mostly VB to V4, with a smaller number of harder problems up to V7. The walk from the parking to the boulders takes roughly 5 to 20 minutes. Emanon holds the most climbs, on big standalone blocks of granite, and mixes easy problems with harder projects. Fern Gully, The Other Side and Anarchy Area come next.

co_wet_mountains_the.blurb: The Wet Mountains lie west of Pueblo and south of Cañon City in southern Colorado, with Westcliffe, Beulah and Florence nearby. Sport leads, followed by trad and a smaller number of boulder problems, mostly in the 5.9 to 5.12 range with 5.10 and 5.11 the most common. The range offers steep sport climbing and multi-pitch trad on granite, and ice is possible in winter. Oak Creek Canyon holds the most climbs, mainly sport on granite from 5.6 to 5.11. Hardscrabble Pass has hard single-pitch sport beside the road and multi-pitch routes on granite spires. Bootlegger's Boulders has 30 to 40 roadside boulders of easy to moderate difficulty. Winters are sheltered from wind, with pleasant climbing on south-facing cliffs.
